issues.summary: Untyped JSONB settings require manual parsing in every consumer
evidence: readChatCloseRatingSettings manually extracts values from JSONB in every call.
issues.suggestion: Define typed Go structs for all settings domains and perform validation/parsing at the ingestion point (e.g., with a dedicated settings management service).

issues.summary: Lack of service layer forces business logic into massive handlers
evidence: chatbot_processor.go contains 2900+ lines of domain logic mixed with HTTP concerns.
issues.suggestion: Extract domain logic into focused service modules with clean interfaces.

issues.summary: Handlers manage everything from I/O to complex business orchestration
evidence: A single method in chatbot_processor.go handles raw events, parses complex JSON, looks up DB settings, and sends external messages.
issues.suggestion: Introduce a Service layer to encapsulate business logic, leaving Handlers to manage only HTTP-specific concerns (status codes, request/response mapping).

issues.summary: Hierarchical settings resolution is manually repeated across handlers
evidence: The logic to check Organization settings and fall back to Instance settings or defaults is reimplemented in every handler that needs it.
issues.suggestion: Extract settings resolution into a focused data-driven utility or service that returns a unified, typed settings object.

issues.summary: internal/handlers is a flat directory with 50+ files
evidence: More than 50 .go files are in one directory, making navigation and ownership tracking difficult.
issues.suggestion: Split internal/handlers into purposeful subdirectories: internal/handlers/auth, internal/handlers/messaging, internal/handlers/workflow, internal/handlers/analytics.

issues.summary: Reusable pkg components depend on private internal models
evidence: pkg/whatsmeow/instance_settings.go imports github.com/compnew2006/whatomate/internal/models.
issues.suggestion: Move the required models to a common/models package or define interfaces in pkg that internal/models implements.

issues.summary: Monstrous handler files (e.g. chatbot_processor.go at 2.9k lines) lack domain decomposition
evidence: chatbot_processor.go exceeds 2900 lines and handles all aspects of chatbot processing in one file.
issues.suggestion: Split monster handlers into domain-aligned service modules or smaller, focused handler sets.

issues.summary: Database initialization hub aggregates too much responsibility
evidence: postgres.go handles connection pool, auto-migration, manual index creation, and seeding of initial data.
issues.suggestion: Move migration and seeding logic to separate packages (e.g., internal/database/migrations and internal/database/seeds).

issues.summary: pkg/ space coupled to internal/models
evidence: pkg/whatsmeow/instance_settings.go imports github.com/compnew2006/whatomate/internal/models.
issues.suggestion: Define shared interfaces or DTOs in pkg/ to decouple from internal models, or move the coupled code to internal/.

issues.summary: Handers contain complex domain logic that should be in a service layer
evidence: Handler methods perform direct DB operations, business logic validation, and third-party integration (Meta API) in one place.
issues.suggestion: Introduce a service layer (e.g., internal/services/) to encapsulate business logic, leaving handlers to focus solely on HTTP orchestration.

issues.summary: Monolithic App struct creates high coupling across all handlers
evidence: Every handler is a method on *App, which carries all system dependencies (DB, Redis, Config, Logic).
issues.suggestion: Refactor App into smaller, capability-focused interfaces or use dependency injection to provide only needed components to specific handlers.

issues.summary: Small utility functions (JSON parsing, form extraction) are duplicated across handlers
evidence: local definitions of parseJSONInt, parseJSONTime, and formValue exist in domain-specific handlers instead of helpers.go.
issues.suggestion: Centralize generic helper functions in internal/handlers/helpers.go or a dedicated internal/pkg/utils package.

issues.summary: Identical logic for resolving org/instance settings is duplicated in many handlers
evidence: Multiple handlers reimplement the logic to fall back from organization settings to instance settings.
issues.suggestion: Create a unified settings resolution helper in the models or a separate settings package.

issues.summary: Identical comment blocks duplicated in pkg/whatsapp/profile_extras.go
evidence: Lines 7-10 contain the same two sentences twice.
issues.suggestion: Remove the duplicated comment block and ensure manual review of AI-generated documentation.

issues.summary: Trivial, restating comments add noise to handler files
evidence: // GetFlow returns a single flow by ID' followed by 'func (a *App) GetFlow'.
issues.suggestion: Replace restating comments with documentation that explains non-obvious behavior, side effects, or business rules, or remove them entirely for trivial methods.

issues.summary: Raw string literals used for domain statuses
evidence: Comparison against 'DEPRECATED', 'PUBLISHED', 'incoming', etc., using literal strings.
issues.suggestion: Define custom types (e.g., type FlowStatus string) and constants for all domain status values.

issues.summary: Pervasive use of untyped JSONB for settings
evidence: Organization.Settings and WhatsAppInstance.Settings are untyped JSONB fields.
issues.suggestion: Define typed setting structs and use GORM's serializer or manual unmarshaling into these types during retrieval.

issues.summary: Giant handler files act as the only layer of extraction for complex domain logic
evidence: chatbot_processor.go aggregates all chatbot logic (2900+ lines) in one file instead of decomposing into specialized sub-processors.
issues.suggestion: Decompose large handlers into smaller, focused internal packages or service modules.

issues.summary: Local helpers for JSON and date parsing are duplicated across handlers
evidence: Multiple files redefine parseJSONInt and similar small helpers.
issues.suggestion: Extract common encoding/parsing logic into a shared internal utility package.

issues.summary: Integration flows are implemented as monolithic blocks instead of collaborator compositions
evidence: Complex multi-step processes are coded as sequential logic within a single receiver method.
issues.suggestion: Refactor complex domain flows into orchestrator services that compose smaller, specialized collaborators.

issues.summary: All internal handoffs are forced through the monolithic App struct
evidence: Every collaborator (DB, Redis, Logger, WhatsApp client) is tied to the App struct, making it impossible to separate concerns at the integration layer.
issues.suggestion: Introduce smaller, interface-based dependency bundles for specific domain subsystems.
